newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei tumbles through key 19,000 level.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei tumbles through key 19,000 level.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key Nikkei 225 average tumbled through the key 19,000 point level just before the market closed on Tuesday.
Dealers said that prices were pushed down by worries over the uncertain outlook for the Japanese economy as buying of blue chips fizzled out.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 average plunged 549.81 points or 2.83 percent to close at 18,896.19. It was the lowest close since December 5, 1995, when the key index finished at 18,879.53.
Its March futures tumbled 610 points to end at 18,880.

The market shrugged off the effects of the yen's recovery against the dollar today. It had previously been hurt by fears that the weak yen might spark foreign investors' sales of their yen-denominated assets, dealers said.
The yen's rebound was sparked by a raft of comments from Japanese officials this morning and late on Monday.
But movements in the currency market had little impact on the stock market.
"I don't think the yen's downtrend will be halted only by verbal intervention," said Tetsuya Ishijima, chief strategist at Okasan Securities Co Ltd.

"The yen's current weakness was backed by Japan's expected weak growth, as were stocks. Unless (Prime Minister Ryutaro) Hashimoto proposes something specific to shore up the economy, the current situation will not change," he said.
Trading volume was light at about 288 million shares on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

Earlier in the morning, Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso also called for a stable currency, saying that wild fluctuations in foreign exchange rates are not welcomed by companies as exchange rates sometimes determine whether the companies can turn a profit.
The dollar, which eased back down after hitting a nearly four-year high of 117 yen in Tokyo on Monday, stood at 115.35/40 yen at 0654 GMT.
Analysts said the downturn in the Nikkei 225 would continue and possibly head towards 18,500, amid a lack of the solid government measures to help the economic recovery.
"There is so much uncertainty about the future of the economy that no one can paint a clear picture," said an analyst at a second-tier securities house.

Shares in Japan's "Big Four" securities houses dropped sharply, adding to the gloomy note in the market. The fall made the brokerage sector 0#SEC.T the second largest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo bourse.
Brokers said the prospect of liberalisation was expected to trigger fierce competition among securities firms.
The share price of Daiwa Securities Co Ltd ended down 75 yen at 955 yen, at the day's low.
Nomura Securities Co Ltd shed 110 yen to end at 1,580 yen, also at the day's low.
Other major losing sectors were fisheries, the largest percentage loser, warehousing, mining and nonferrous metals.
There were no notable gaining sectors, but a limited number of blue chips continued to retain a firm tone, brokers said.
The second section index ended down 2.94 points at 1,826.27, with 7.19 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 5.95 points at 1,327.16.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
